title: UniProt: the Universal Protein Knowledgebase in 2025
funder: National Human Genome Research Institute [HG002273]; NIH Office of the Director [U24HG007822]; NIAID; NIA; NIGMS [R35GM141873]; NIDDK; NEI; NCI; NHLBI; BBSRC [BB/T015608/1]; National Science Foundation Directorate for Biological Sciences [BB/X002179/1]; Open Targets; Horizon 2020 [825575]; Swiss State Secretariat for Education, Research and Innovation; EMBL Australia.
result: Reviewed UniProtKB entries, release 2026_03, read through rest.uniprot.org. REN (P00797), renin: a highly specific endopeptidase whose only known function is to generate angiotensin I from angiotensinogen in the plasma; cleavage of the Leu-|-Xaa bond in angiotensinogen (EC 3.4.23.15); secreted; interaction with ATP6AP2 gives a 5-fold higher efficiency of angiotensinogen processing; variants cause renal tubular dysgenesis and autosomal dominant tubulointerstitial kidney disease 4. AGT (P01019), angiotensinogen: expressed by the liver and secreted in plasma; renin cleaves it to angiotensin-1, from which ACE removes a dipeptide to yield angiotensin-2; angiotensin-2 acts on AGTR1 and AGTR2, constricts vascular smooth muscle and stimulates aldosterone release; angiotensin 1-7 has been proposed to be cleaved from angiotensin-2 by ACE2 or from angiotensin-1 by neprilysin (MME) and has vasodilator and antidiuretic effects through MAS1; variants are associated with susceptibility to essential hypertension and cause renal tubular dysgenesis. ACE (P12821): a dipeptidyl carboxypeptidase (EC 3.4.15.1) composed of two similar catalytic domains, each with a functional active site and different substrate selectivity; angiotensin I + H2O = L-histidyl-L-leucine + angiotensin II; bradykinin + H2O = L-Phe-L-Arg + bradykinin(1-7); binds 2 Zn2+ and 3 chloride ions per subunit; the dipeptidyl carboxypeptidase activity is strongly activated by chloride and specifically inhibited by lisinopril, captopril and enalaprilat; cleavage of angiotensin I and cholecystokinin is mediated by the C-terminal catalytic region, degradation of N-acetyl-SDKP and of amyloid-beta peptides by the N-terminal domain; also degrades substance P, neurotensin and enkephalins; ubiquitously expressed, with highest levels in lung, kidney, heart, gastrointestinal system and prostate; a soluble form is released after cleavage in the juxtamembrane stalk; the testis-specific isoform contains only one catalytic domain and is required for male fertility; genetic variants in ACE are associated with interindividual variability of plasma ACE levels; variants cause renal tubular dysgenesis. AGTR1 (P30556), type-1 angiotensin II receptor: receptor for angiotensin II; the activated receptor couples to G-alpha proteins G(q) (GNAQ, GNA11, GNA14 or GNA15), activates phospholipase C and raises cytosolic Ca2+, which stimulates protein kinase C; cell membrane; variants cause renal tubular dysgenesis. ACE2 (Q9BYF1): counter-regulatory carboxypeptidase of the renin-angiotensin system; angiotensin II + H2O = angiotensin-(1-7) + L-phenylalanine (EC 3.4.17.23) and angiotensin I + H2O = angiotensin-(1-9) + L-leucine; binds 1 Zn2+ and 1 chloride ion per subunit; not inhibited by the ACE inhibitors lisinopril, captopril and enalaprilat. CYP2C9 (P11712): a cytochrome P450 monooxygenase of the endoplasmic reticulum membrane that inserts one oxygen atom into a substrate and reduces the second to water, with two electrons provided by NADPH through cytochrome P450 reductase; contributes to the wide pharmacokinetic variability of the metabolism of S-warfarin, diclofenac, phenytoin, tolbutamide and losartan.
